notes: Hand-derived before the detector ran, under the Prism lexer normalisation in ruby_lex.rs (names $id, literals $lit with a string as one token, comments and newlines dropped): five-token shingles, both bodies at least eighty tokens, shared shingles at least seventy percent of the smaller body's.
exact_a / exact_b: verbatim twins, about ninety-two tokens each, so shingles_a == shingles_b == shared (containment 1.00). Over fifty tokens and five lines, so the same pair is also a clone group.

near_a / near_b: near_b is near_a with `return out if values.empty?` (six tokens) inserted after the three assignments and `total = total.abs` (five tokens) inserted between the largest and count writes, so shingles_b - shingles_a == 11. Each insertion breaks the four windows that straddle it; a broken window is lost unless the same normalised window occurs elsewhere in the body, so shared is under shingles_a but the exact loss is pinned from the first run. No equal run reaches fifty tokens, so there is no clone group.
prefix_a / prefix_b: `def $id ( $id ) $id = $lit $id = $lit` is shared, then an each-block against a case: containment far under seventy percent, no pair.
small_a / small_b: identical but about twelve tokens: no pair, no clone group.
observed: near pair integers from the first run on 2026-09-15, pinned as a regression; a change to the token rules or the thresholds moves them and must say so.
